advisor_identified: Béatrice Craig, historian of rural Canadian social and economic history at the University of Ottawa; supervisor of Denise Jacques’s 2010 furniture-history dissertation.

doctorate.title: Family, Kinship, and Community Formation on the Canadian-American Border: Madawaska, 1785-1842

evidence.says: University of Ottawa faculty profile identifies Béatrice Craig as professor emeritus in History and lists a Ph.D. from the University of Maine in 1983.

Acadian Archives finding aid for Craig’s research collection, biographical sketch (p. 4), states that she received her Ph.D. in Canadian and American History from the University of Maine in 1983 and became an Ottawa history professor in 1985. Inventory item 734 identifies her Madawaska dissertation under the name Béatrice Chevalier Craig, with the matching title, as a history Ph.D. thesis at the University of Maine at Orono, 1983.

Université de Moncton’s ACADIE bibliographic guide, entry 1138 (PDF p. 81), records Béatrice Chevalier Craig’s Family, kinship and community formation on the Canadian-American border: Madawaska, 1785-1842 as a Ph.D. thesis, University of Maine, Orono, 1983.

Denise Jacques’s Decent Furniture for Decent People dissertation has a University of Ottawa, 2010, history Ph.D. title page; its abstract page (p. ii) pairs Jacques’s name with Béatrice Craig, confirming the advisor identity associated with the student in the entry.

notes: The linked AHA record matches the independently documented institution, year, history discipline and dissertation title. The archival inventory uses the fuller author name Béatrice Chevalier Craig.
